tasks.task: Cost a recipe and build a recipe card

items.when: When you have recipes and supplier invoices and need cost per portion with trim and yield
When one batch of one dish must be costed from real weights and what was paid
When a card mixes grams, litres and each, to check the units and how rough the figure is
When the cards live in a spreadsheet, to find formula errors and broken links
When a yield or portion size is a guess and should be tested by changing one thing

tasks.task: Set menu prices that hit a target food cost

items.when: When costed cards exist and each dish needs a price for the target food cost percent
When weighing a price, to decide on rounding, how to price extras and where to show it
Before a price change, to see what the margin allows and the wording to use
When regulars or catering clients must be told about a rise and you want to keep them

tasks.task: Review which dishes earn their place on the menu

items.when: When you have the till's sales mix and need a keep, reprice, rework or cut call per dish
When you want each item's margin and the ones that lose money shown plainly
Before the review goes to the owner, to check totals and state the key figures in plain words
When the numbers say cut a dish and nobody has asked the floor staff or the guests

tasks.task: Run a weekly food cost check

items.when: When the week's purchases, stock and sales are in and you need actual food cost percent
When actual cost is above the recipe cost, to split the gap into price, volume and waste
When margin fell this week, to rank the likely causes before blaming portions
When food cost creeps up every month and each fix only holds for a week

tasks.task: Close the month's food cost after the stock count

items.when: Each month, within a few days of the stock count, to run the close in order
When counts are slow or wrong, to set who counts what and how to trace mismatches
When the count must be valued at what was paid, with write-downs flagged
When the count and the records disagree, to split timing, unit and counting errors
Before the close, to match the month's invoices and list amounts to query

tasks.task: Check supplier price changes and compare suppliers

items.when: When an invoice or price list shows new prices and you need the effect on each dish
When quotes use different pack sizes and units and must be compared like for like
When total spend is too high, to get a sourcing plan and a supplier shortlist
When an invoice looks wrong, to recalculate every line and total
When a delivery does not match the order, to get a mismatch table and supplier questions

tasks.task: Write opening and closing checklists by area

items.when: When each area needs its tasks listed in the order they happen
Before the checklists, to write one page of checkable standards for how the place should feel
When the list is drafted, to cut each line to words a new starter reads at a glance
When standards change with whoever is on shift and the basics were never written down

tasks.task: Set daily prep lists and par levels

items.when: When dishes run out on busy nights and prep is thrown away on quiet ones
When the pars must become a daily prep list each station can follow
When you have past sales, to forecast covers and track how far off the forecast runs
When batch items are made weekly, to plan amounts from past sales and kitchen capacity
When a special uses a short-life ingredient, to pick the order amount and see the risk

tasks.task: Write one-page station guides for kitchen and floor

items.when: When each station needs set-up, service and clean-down on one page
When you have a standards sheet, to get a job card for each role and a day-one trial sheet
When one task, such as cashing up, needs a written procedure with the edge cases
When a new starter has read the guide, to check they took in the points that matter

tasks.task: Set up a shift log and handover

items.when: At the end of a shift, to brief the next lead with food safety issues first
When shift notes pile up, to keep an open-issue list and what to escalate
When the venue has no shift log template and needs one that fits its areas
When the log's fields must feed the weekly review without retyping

tasks.task: Run the weekly restaurant review

items.when: Every week on the same quiet day, to run the review and set the week's actions
When shift log, till, bookings, waste log and reviews must become one page
When the owner wants the same numbers each week with a trend and a forecast
When the week's reviews and comment cards need sorting into themes
When covers or spend per head fell, to rank the causes by evidence

tasks.task: Reply to a batch of online reviews

items.when: When new Google, booking or delivery app reviews need replies
When reviews arrive every week, to hold risky ones back and flag repeat complaints
When a reply has the right facts but the wrong tone, to try it warmer or firmer
Before posting, to check no reply promises a refund or change nobody agreed
When replies defend the kitchen and miss what the guest's evening was like

tasks.task: Handle a direct guest complaint

items.when: When a guest writes to complain, to get a warm reply, a fair fix and who to tell
When the guest is furious, to try a reply that names the feeling first
Before sending, to test each promise against what the manager may offer

tasks.task: Draft next week's rota against forecast covers

items.when: When building next week's rota so hours follow the covers
When busy hours must be covered within staff limits, with a cost check per shift
When weekends and lates feel unfair, to try a rotation with a swap policy
After the week, to total hours worked and flag every oddity against the rota
When lateness and no-shows have no written rule

tasks.task: Draft an allergen matrix from recipe cards

items.when: When a menu, special or recipe changes and the trained manager needs a draft to check
Before the matrix, to make sure every recipe card lists each ingredient and sub-recipe
When the matrix is drafted, to tie each allergen to a dated supplier spec or mark it open

tasks.task: Launch a new or seasonal menu

items.when: When a seasonal change, new opening or menu rework must run from costing to first service
When several versions of a dish are in play, to plan a tasting with a decision rule
When dish descriptions are vague, to make each short, true and easy to picture
When the printed menu needs a new look, to see three layouts at real size and pick one
When floor staff must learn the new dishes, to plan the briefing minute by minute
When the menu is drafted, to read it as a guest and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Cost and check a catering or event order

items.when: Before the event, to match the order to the quote and details and list what to ask the client
When the event menu needs a cost per head and a price
When staff, travel and hire costs are added, to see the profit on this one order
When the client asks for allergen information for the event dishes

tasks.task: Cut food waste and track it

items.when: When you want a cost on each step and a price on each kind of waste
When stock goes out of date, to get a use-first list and when to run it as a special
When the kitchen's flow causes the waste, to map it and rank quick fixes by payoff
Each week, to see whether the waste log is moving after a change

tasks.task: Plan stock orders and the cash to pay for them

items.when: When dry goods and drinks need reorder points and safety stock from sales
Before ordering fresh goods, to take the pars by day of week
When supplier bills bunch up, to see the next 30, 60 and 90 days of cash
Before a quiet season, to test a downside case and set actions

tasks.task: Hire and train new kitchen and floor staff

items.when: When a role is open, to write a clear post with real requirements
Before interviews, to get set questions, answer signs and a scorecard
When someone starts, to plan a day-by-day first week with one small real task
When training must follow the station guide the starter will work from
At the end of week one, to check what stuck and what to go over again

tasks.task: Plan specials, set menus and offers that keep margin

items.when: Before choosing an offer, to see which dishes have the margin to carry it
When you want a bundle or added-value idea in place of a plain price cut
When the offer needs a name, to get ten and the three to test
Before it runs, to find the deepest discount the margin allows

tasks.task: Find what slows service and fix ticket times

items.when: When tickets back up, to map the steps and find the one stage holding service up
When weighing an extra pass, grill or runner, to test the change before paying for it
When breakdowns cause the delays, to set a service schedule and spares list
The week after a change, to see whether ticket times moved

tasks.task: Get the operation ready for a new opening or second site

items.when: When the owner wants a second site, to see if the first runs without them
When the best site's ways must become standards and a manual a stranger can follow
When the guest experience must feel the same in both places
Before copying the system, to try it in one place and check the costs first

always.when: Before any checklist, card or menu is printed, to catch typos and dish names spelt two ways
When a document states a price, a yield or a food safety rule, to tie it to a dated source

helpers.when: When a dish needs developing, scaling or testing, not only costing
When the job is filling quiet nights, listings, bookings and social, not running service
When the venue needs a food safety system, risk assessments or an incident log
When supplier contracts must be tendered or renegotiated across the whole spend
When the printed menu, menu board or table cards need laying out for print
When contracts, tips rules, breaks or a staff dispute need handling properly

gaps: No library item runs menu engineering: sorting dishes by margin and popularity from the till's sales mix
No library item builds a costed recipe card with trim and cooking yield, sub-recipes and food cost percent
No library item works out actual against theoretical food cost from stock counts and sales
No library item writes opening and closing checklists, prep lists or station guides for a kitchen or bar
No library item drafts an allergen matrix or covers calories and menu labelling rules
No library item covers food safety records such as temperature logs, cleaning schedules or a HACCP plan
No library item drafts a rota against forecast covers or checks labour cost as a share of sales
No library item covers tips and service charge sharing, or cash-up and till variance
No library item plans a menu's sections and dish order, or writes dish descriptions in several styles to compare
No library item covers bookings: no-show rules, deposits, table turn times or delivery app fees and pricing
No library item costs drinks: pour cost, cocktail specs or a wine list margin check
No thinking lens covers hospitality and restaurant service
